summary: Cocke County tower site (4,314 ft) listed as removed from Cherokee National Forest; a Forest Service campground of that name sits at 3,100 ft.

facts.status_note: Tower removed. No source describes what, if anything, remains at the site.

evidence.supports: CNF stands for Cherokee National Forest
evidence.quote: The Cherokee National Forest (CNF) had 18 fire towers.

evidence.supports: campground near the top of Round Mountain in Cocke County
evidence.quote: This campground is located near the top of Round Mountain in Cocke County.
Situated at 3,100 feet, it is one of the highest-elevation campgrounds in Cherokee National Forest.
Round Mountain is a first-come first-served campground.
Reservations cannot be made online at this time.

sources.title: TN lookout tower: COT005 Round Mountain
Round Mountain Campground
sources.publisher: USDA Forest Service, Cherokee National Forest

notes_for_editor: Only the tnlandforms list gives the tower's elevation, removal and Cherokee National Forest tie; no build date, staffing or fire history found after two web searches and the cached tnlandforms, Cocke County history and Forest Service pages. The campground page describes a campground, not the tower, and does not say it shares the tower site. Elevations disagree: 4,314 ft for the tower per tnlandforms, 3,100 ft for the campground per the Forest Service. The tnlandforms 'cnf' abbreviation is read as Cherokee National Forest from the list's own note that CNF is Cherokee National Forest.
